Under steady load a Node server can sit at about 12 times its live heap and stay there. On a stress test of 100k keys per page, a live heap of 90 MB ran at about 1.1 GB of RSS. This is not a leak. After one oversized GC cycle V8 raises its heap limit, and it keeps the freed pages in a pool for reuse while load lasts. About 8 seconds after load stops the pool empties and RSS falls to about 160 MB.

After a failure the limit is 250 ms until the store answers again. Three failures in a row close the layer for 5 seconds. While it is closed, and while a read has just failed, nothing is written. A failed write closes nothing, so a read-only replica keeps serving reads. A store whose answers take longer than these limits counts as failing: a miss, and the dictionary comes from its source. With ioredis that starts near 400 ms per command, because its handshake takes three round trips. The module logs one warning per minute; ioredis prints its own errors on top of that. A value that is not a dictionary counts as a miss and is overwritten. An unknown mount name warns once on first use; the app then runs without the layer.
